title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed (Positive)

Volatility remains elevated as the major indices continue to slop around. On Thursday, large caps broke out of their short-term ranges, only to be hit with distribution on Friday ahead of the long weekend. Mid- and small-cap indices, meanwhile, continue to chop sideways following their large surges from August 22. As of this writing, futures suggest a weaker open following Labor Day, which could place the indices in a more vulnerable state and call for tactical adjustments.

Breadth and momentum remain stable overall, but have been waning since last week. The contraction in new highs versus new lows, along with a narrowing skew between upside and downside momentum, signals fading participation. This is an important development to monitor, as it becomes increasingly difficult to sustain long-side momentum when fewer stocks are making new highs.

On the sector front, leadership has rotated. The top five groups are now Materials, Consumer Cyclical, Healthcare, Financials, and Energy. Notably, Technology has dropped out of the top five after leading the market for several months. This rotation underscores why the tape has felt sloppy and volatile, as leadership disperses and traders search for new themes. Going forward, attention should remain on which groups consolidate their leadership and provide fresh direction for the broader market.

Plan of Action

1. Trend Alignment

  • All four major indices remain above intermediate-term moving averages (20/50-day), but distribution and weak opens are eroding short-term strength.

  • Treat large-cap weakness (SPY/QQQ) as a cautionary signal, while mids and smalls holding sideways is only neutral—not yet constructive.

  • If mid/small caps break below their 20-day MAs on volume, reduce long exposure materially.

2. Breadth & Momentum

  • Breadth and momentum are stable but fading, with fewer stocks making new highs.

  • Until breadth re-expands, limit position count and keep trade expectancy realistic.

  • Watch for a decisive breadth thrust or contraction in new lows as signals for shifting posture.

3. Sector Allocation

  • Current leaders: Materials, Consumer Cyclical, Healthcare, Financials, Energy.

  • Technology has fallen out of the top tier, confirming a rotation. Reduce exposure in extended Tech names and monitor for stabilization.

  • Stay diversified across cyclical and defensive leaders, rather than concentrated in one theme.

4. Stock Selection & Breakout Strategy

  • Continue applying the breakout playbook:

    • Look for leaders from top sectors with stair-step patterns: strong run → orderly consolidation → breakout.

    • Enter on breakout above consolidation highs; stops just below day’s lows or consolidation support, no wider than ATR/ADR.

  • Avoid extended or sloppy setups. In volatile tapes, only take tight consolidations with rising MAs underneath.

  • Keep position sizing modest (½–¾ normal) until breadth and trend stabilize.

5. Risk Management & Cash Levels

  • Raise cash buffer to 30–40% given high volatility and narrowing internals.

  • Scale profits quickly: take ⅓–½ off after 3–5 days or a fast 5–10% gain, then trail remainder with 10- or 20-day MA.

  • Move stops to breakeven quickly after partials to remove downside risk in a choppy environment.

6. Scenario Planning

  • Bullish: If breadth expands (new highs > new lows for multiple sessions) and indices reclaim breakout levels with volume, selectively add risk in leading sectors.

  • Neutral: If chop persists, maintain light exposure in relative strength names, but prioritize cash.

  • Bearish: If mids/smalls join large caps in breaking support, broaden cash levels to 50%+ and reduce long bias until fresh bases appear.
